title: The Sodium That Flows On
endLine: Sodium missed upstream reaches ENaC, and more potassium is secreted.

scenes.tts: A kidney tubule pulls sodium back all along its length. Close one sodium door near the middle, and more potassium leaves in the urine, farther down. Why potassium?
scenes.narration: A kidney tubule pulls sodium back all along its length. Close one sodium door near the middle, and more potassium leaves in the urine, farther down. Why potassium?
scenes.caption: A kidney tubule pulls sodium back all along its length. Close one sodium door near the middle, and more potassium leaves in the urine, farther down. Why potassium?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene and in the second film: sodium YELLOW dots; potassium MAGENTA dots; the sodium-potassium pump RED; tubule segments by colour: proximal tubule TEAL, thick ascending limb ORANGE, distal convoluted tubule PURPLE, collecting duct BLUE; charge signs (plus, minus) bright WHITE; tubular fluid pale. LAYOUT: one long kidney tubule drawn left to right across the upper two thirds of the frame, filling about 60% of frame height, as a wide straight band split into four coloured segments in that order (schematic, no anatomy, no loop shape). Its upper inner surface is the lumen, filled with pale fluid in which YELLOW dots flow slowly left to right. Its lower wall is a row of simple cells; below the cells a dark band labelled 'body side'. At the right end the tube empties into a small cup labelled 'urine'. Along the bottom of the frame, a single horizontal bar, empty for now. A small 'schematic' tag at bottom right stays all film. HOOK MOTION: YELLOW dots leave the lumen down through the cells into the body side all along the tube. On 'Close one sodium door', a small ORANGE gate in the orange segment's top wall slides shut and glows. More YELLOW dots now stream on past it to the right. On 'more potassium', in the BLUE segment, MAGENTA dots begin to rise out of the cells into the lumen and flow into the urine cup. On the question, large white text across the top: 'Why potassium?'

Title 'The Sodium That Flows On' fades in above the tube for 2 s while 'Why potassium?' fades out. The ORANGE gate slides open again (reset to normal); MAGENTA stream in the blue segment returns to a thin trickle. YELLOW dots keep flowing and leaving through the walls.

scenes.tts: Filtered fluid flows along the tube. Each stretch takes sodium back through its own door. The door sits on the apical side, the side facing the fluid.
scenes.narration: Filtered fluid flows along the tube. Each stretch takes sodium back through its own door. The door sits on the apical side, the side facing the fluid.
scenes.caption: Filtered fluid flows along the tube. Each stretch takes sodium back through its own door. The door sits on the apical side, the side facing the fluid.
scenes.visual: Slow push-in on one cell in the TEAL segment until the cell fills about 65% of frame height; the neighbouring cells stay visible at the edges, the lumen above, the body side below. YELLOW dots drift past in the lumen. On 'its own door', a door shape in the cell's top membrane glows TEAL and YELLOW dots pass down through it into the cell. On 'apical side', the top membrane brightens to a thick WHITE line, labelled 'apical: faces fluid'.

scenes.tts: Every door runs on the same engine. On the basolateral side, facing the surrounding tissue, the sodium potassium pump exports sodium. That keeps sodium low inside, so it flows in.
scenes.narration: Every door runs on the same engine. On the basolateral side, facing the surrounding tissue, the sodium-potassium pump exports sodium. That keeps sodium low inside, so it flows in.
scenes.caption: Every door runs on the same engine. On the basolateral side, facing the surrounding tissue, the sodium-potassium pump exports sodium. That keeps sodium low inside, so it flows in.
scenes.visual: Same cell. On 'basolateral side', the base and sides of the cell brighten to a darker SLATE line, labelled 'basolateral'. A RED pump cartoon appears in the base, labelled 'Na+-K+ pump'. It turns steadily, throwing YELLOW dots out of the base into the body side. The YELLOW dots inside the cell stay few; on 'so it flows in', YELLOW dots keep entering through the TEAL door at the top. The pump keeps turning for the rest of the film, in every cell, whenever cells are on screen.

scenes.tts: Along the tube, the doors change. The proximal tubule uses N H E three and S G L T two. The thick ascending limb uses N K C C two. The distal convoluted tubule uses N C C. The collecting duct uses E N a C.
scenes.narration: Along the tube, the doors change. The proximal tubule uses NHE3 and SGLT2. The thick ascending limb uses NKCC2. The distal convoluted tubule uses NCC. The collecting duct uses ENaC.
scenes.caption: Along the tube, the doors change. The proximal tubule uses NHE3 and SGLT2. The thick ascending limb uses NKCC2. The distal convoluted tubule uses NCC. The collecting duct uses ENaC.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole tube. Each segment's top wall shows one door in its segment colour, each a different simple shape, and each lights as it is named, with a label of its name only: TEAL 'NHE3, SGLT2', ORANGE 'NKCC2', PURPLE 'NCC', BLUE 'ENaC'. Under every segment, a small RED pump turns in the cell bases, all identical, to show the one shared engine. YELLOW dots keep flowing and leaving through each door.

scenes.tts: They take very different shares. In rounded human estimates, the proximal tubule takes back about sixty-five percent of filtered sodium. The thick limb takes about twenty-five. The distal convoluted tubule takes about five, and the collecting duct about three.
scenes.narration: They take very different shares. In rounded human estimates, the proximal tubule takes back about 65% of filtered sodium. The thick limb takes about 25. The distal convoluted tubule takes about 5, and the collecting duct about 3.
scenes.caption: They take very different shares. In rounded human estimates, the proximal tubule takes back about 65% of filtered sodium. The thick limb takes about 25. The distal convoluted tubule takes about 5, and the collecting duct about 3.
scenes.visual: The empty bar at the bottom fills from left to right in four coloured blocks whose widths are 65, 25, 5 and 3 units, one block per segment as each is named, labelled '65%', '25%', '5%', '3%' (the last two labels sit just above their thin blocks). Tag above the bar: 'rounded human estimates'. The blocks are not drawn to sum to 100 and the leftover space is left unlabelled. In the tube, the stream of YELLOW dots in the lumen visibly thins from left to right as each segment takes its share.

scenes.tts: Each door brings sodium in its own way, so a different drug can block each one. Furosemide, a loop diuretic, blocks N K C C two in the thick limb.
scenes.narration: Each door brings sodium in its own way, so a different drug can block each one. Furosemide, a loop diuretic, blocks NKCC2 in the thick limb.
scenes.caption: Each door brings sodium in its own way, so a different drug can block each one. Furosemide, a loop diuretic, blocks NKCC2 in the thick limb.
scenes.visual: Each coloured door gets a small matching padlock outline that hovers near it, unlocked (a door can be blocked, schematic). On 'Furosemide', the padlock over the ORANGE door closes onto it, labelled 'furosemide'. The orange door goes dark and no YELLOW dots pass through it. The '25%' block in the bar starts to pulse.

scenes.tts: Block that door, and up to about a quarter of filtered sodium flows on. The segments downstream normally take back only about eight percent between them.
scenes.narration: Block that door, and up to about a quarter of filtered sodium flows on. The segments downstream normally take back only about 8% between them.
scenes.caption: Block that door, and up to about a quarter of filtered sodium flows on. The segments downstream normally take back only about 8% between them.
scenes.visual: In the lumen, the YELLOW stream that used to thin at the orange segment now runs on thick into the purple and blue segments. In the bar, the pulsing ORANGE '25%' block slides right, past the end of the purple and blue blocks, labelled 'flows on: up to ~25%'. The PURPLE '5%' and BLUE '3%' blocks glow together under a bracket labelled 'downstream: ~8%'. The orange block is visibly much wider than the bracket.

scenes.tts: That extra sodium flows on to E N a C, in the late distal tubule and collecting duct. And E N a C lets sodium in alone, with no partner ion.
scenes.narration: That extra sodium flows on to ENaC, in the late distal tubule and collecting duct. And ENaC lets sodium in alone, with no partner ion.
scenes.caption: That extra sodium flows on to ENaC, in the late distal tubule and collecting duct. And ENaC lets sodium in alone, with no partner ion.
scenes.visual: Camera glides right along the tube and pushes in on one cell of the BLUE segment until it fills about 65% of frame height, lumen above, body side below, RED pump turning in its base. The extra YELLOW dots arrive crowded in the lumen. The BLUE ENaC door, a simple open channel, lets YELLOW dots drop through one at a time; each YELLOW dot carries a small WHITE plus sign. Nothing enters with them: label 'sodium alone'.

scenes.tts: So positive charge is leaving the fluid, with nothing to balance it. What happens to the charge of the fluid left behind?
scenes.narration: So positive charge is leaving the fluid, with nothing to balance it. What happens to the charge of the fluid left behind?
scenes.caption: So positive charge is leaving the fluid, with nothing to balance it. What happens to the charge of the fluid left behind?
scenes.visual: WHITE plus signs ride down through the ENaC door with each YELLOW dot. The lumen fluid above is shown with a blank charge meter at the right edge, needle at zero, labelled 'lumen charge'. Question card across the top in white: 'What charge is left behind?'

Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: YELLOW dots bob in the crowded lumen, the BLUE channel shimmers faintly, the meter needle trembles at zero. The RED pump turns slowly.

scenes.tts: It goes negative. That negative lumen drives potassium out of the cell and into the urine. It leaves through a potassium channel called R O M K.
scenes.narration: It goes negative. That negative lumen drives potassium out of the cell and into the urine. It leaves through a potassium channel called ROMK.
scenes.caption: It goes negative. That negative lumen drives potassium out of the cell and into the urine. It leaves through a potassium channel called ROMK.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. WHITE minus signs appear scattered through the lumen fluid; the meter needle swings to 'negative' (no number, schematic). A second door opens in the cell's top membrane, a MAGENTA channel labelled 'ROMK'. MAGENTA potassium dots inside the cell rise through it into the lumen, drawn toward the minus signs, and flow right toward the urine cup at the edge of frame.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Every segment has its own sodium door, and every door runs on one pump. Block an upstream door, and the sodium it misses reaches E N a C. More potassium is secreted.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Every segment has its own sodium door, and every door runs on one pump. Block an upstream door, and the sodium it misses reaches ENaC. More potassium is secreted.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Every segment has its own sodium door, and every door runs on one pump. Block an upstream door, and the sodium it misses reaches ENaC. More potassium is secreted.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole tube. On 'its own sodium door', the four coloured doors light in turn; on 'one pump', all the RED pumps pulse together. On 'Block an upstream door', the padlocked ORANGE door glows; a thick YELLOW stream runs from it to the BLUE segment, where a MAGENTA stream rises into the lumen and pours into the urine cup. White text across the top: 'Missed sodium costs potassium'.

scenes.tts: How much potassium depends on how much extra sodium and flow arrive. And aldosterone, raised by sustained salt loss, adds to the effect.
scenes.narration: How much potassium depends on how much extra sodium and flow arrive. And aldosterone, raised by sustained salt loss, adds to the effect.
scenes.caption: How much potassium depends on how much extra sodium and flow arrive. And aldosterone, raised by sustained salt loss, adds to the effect.
scenes.visual: Same whole-tube view. A simple slider at the top left labelled 'sodium arriving' moves from low to high; as it rises, the YELLOW stream into the blue segment thickens and the MAGENTA stream into the urine cup thickens with it (schematic, no numbers). On 'aldosterone', a small BLUE-WHITE hormone drop labelled 'aldosterone' drifts onto the blue segment, which brightens, and the MAGENTA stream thickens a little more.

scenes.tts: So a sodium door is never only about sodium. Whatever it misses, the tube downstream has to handle, and potassium pays the price.
scenes.narration: So a sodium door is never only about sodium. Whatever it misses, the tube downstream has to handle, and potassium pays the price.
scenes.caption: So a sodium door is never only about sodium. Whatever it misses, the tube downstream has to handle, and potassium pays the price.
scenes.visual: The slider and hormone drop fade. Slow pan along the tube from the padlocked ORANGE door, following the YELLOW stream right to the BLUE segment, and on to the MAGENTA stream falling into the urine cup, which fills slightly. The padlock and the four coloured doors stay visible.

End card over the dimmed tube, large white text, centred: 'Sodium missed upstream reaches ENaC, and more potassium is secreted.' YELLOW dots still flow slowly along the lumen and MAGENTA dots trickle into the urine cup behind it.
